description: Minimal Blazor component tree: a base component, a layout that inherits it, a component carrying two @implements directives whose interfaces are declared in a C# file beside it, and a component with no hierarchy directive at all. Exercises component extraction, component->event-handler CONTAINS, and — the reason the fixture exists (#6370) — the @inherits and @implements directives, including the three places razor text LOOKS like a directive and must NOT produce an edge: mid-line markup, a one-line @* *@ comment, and a multi-line one.

expected_entities.name: AppLayoutBase
expected_entities.note: The base MainLayout inherits. It declares no directive of its own — a base component is also a plain component. The subtype is load-bearing here and on every component row below: SCOPE.UIComponent is ALSO the kind razor gives an @inject entity (`Js` in Counter.razor), so a kind-only row is satisfied by a record that is not a component at all.

expected_entities.name: MainLayout
expected_entities.note: The @inherits owner. Its name comes from the FILE PATH (componentNameFromPath never reads the file), which is why the hierarchy edge has to be anchored on this record rather than on a node the cross/hierarchy pass would mint.

expected_entities.name: NavMenu
expected_entities.note: The @implements owner — two directives, one component.

expected_entities.name: Counter
expected_entities.note: The negative control: no hierarchy directive, and three decoys that look like one. It must keep every entity and edge it had before #6370 while acquiring no hierarchy edge.

expected_entities.name: IAppDisposable
expected_entities.note: The C# interface NavMenu implements. Present so the IMPLEMENTS edge below has a real node at the far end: without it the row would be graded on a dangling target, and per #6947 a dangling edge still de-orphans its source, so the orphan metric could never tell the difference.

expected_entities.name: IAppTrackable
expected_entities.note: The second interface — the far end of the row that grades directive MULTIPLICITY.

expected_relationships.note: #6370: `@inherits AppLayoutBase`. The razor->razor case, and the only row that grades EXTENDS at all. FROM is the component in MainLayout.razor and TO is the component in a DIFFERENT file, so a producer that anchored the edge on the file entity, or that resolved the target within the owning file only, fails here.

#6370: FIRST `@implements` directive, and the CROSS-LANGUAGE case — the interface is declared in C#, which is where a Blazor component's interfaces actually live. Held constant with the row below except for which directive line it came from.

#6370: SECOND `@implements` directive on the SAME component. This is the only row that grades multiplicity — Razor spells multiple interfaces as repeated directive LINES, not as a comma list, so a producer that took the first match (FindStringSubmatch rather than FindAll) satisfies the row above and fails this one.

Pre-existing razor behaviour on the component that also carries hierarchy edges: the @code block's event handler. Held so a regression that dropped ALL embedded relationships is distinguishable from one that dropped only the hierarchy kinds — both would otherwise read the same way.
The same pre-existing behaviour on the component with NO hierarchy directive: Counter must keep its member edge while acquiring no EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS.

forbidden_relationships.note:
#6370 OVER-FIRING, the line-leading anchor: Counter.razor's markup contains `

A directive is line-leading; @inherits WraithBase here is markup text.

`. A directive is only a directive at the start of its line. FIRES, verified: deleting the `^` from reInherits produces exactly Counter -> WraithBase and the gate reports one forbidden hit.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, one-line Razor comment: `@* @inherits GhostBase *@`. Note this decoy is NOT line-leading either, so the anchor alone rejects it and it does not grade the scrub on its own — it is the pair to the row below, which is the one that does. FIRES, verified: with BOTH the `^` anchor and scrubRazorComments removed, this row and WraithBase fire together.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, MULTI-LINE Razor comment — the row that grades scrubRazorComments by itself. `@implements IPhantom` sits at column 0 on its own line INSIDE a `@*` … `*@` block, so it is line-leading and the anchor cannot reject it: the scrub is the only thing that does. FIRES, verified: disabling scrubRazorComments alone (returning src unchanged) produces exactly Counter -> IPhantom, with the anchor left intact.

#6370 KIND EXCLUSIVITY, @inherits half. `@inherits` is single inheritance and is EXTENDS, never IMPLEMENTS. Emitting both kinds costs nothing in recall — the must_exist EXTENDS row still binds — so the exclusivity is ungraded in the permissive direction unless it is fenced here. FIRES, verified: changing add("EXTENDS", reInherits) to add("IMPLEMENTS", reInherits) fails the must_exist row AND registers this forbidden hit; adding a second add("IMPLEMENTS", reInherits) beside the first keeps recall at 100% and is caught by this row ALONE.

#6370 KIND EXCLUSIVITY, @implements half — the mirror of the row above, so the two directives are fenced independently rather than one standing in for both. FIRES, verified: an extra add("EXTENDS", reImplements) leaves every must_exist row satisfied and is caught only here.

forbidden_entities.name: AppLayoutBase
forbidden_entities.note: #6370: THE failure mode of the rejected implementation route. Registering razor in cross/hierarchy's supportedLanguages mints a SCOPE.Component for the type AND one for each parent, so the base named by MainLayout's directive would appear a second time, as a Component attributed to MainLayout.razor, with the edge anchored on it instead of on the real component. The genuine AppLayoutBase is a SCOPE.UIComponent in its OWN file (must_exist above), so the two rows cannot be satisfied by the same record. FIRES, verified — and this row's previous note said the opposite, which was the wrong direction of the same defect the notes elsewhere in this file guard against: it claimed the row was unreachable 'since this extractor mints entities only from file paths'. A review's mutant minting a SCOPE.Component from each hierarchy TARGET rather than from the path produced exactly this row, forb_ent 1: `AppLayoutBase [SCOPE.Component] in Components/Layout/MainLayout.razor`. The row is graded, not aspirational. What it still does NOT observe is the ROUTE — registering razor in supportedLanguages would not run this extractor differently at all; the fence is on the SHAPE that route produces.

forbidden_entities.name: GhostBase
forbidden_entities.note: #6370: the base named inside Counter.razor's one-line Razor comment. REACHABLE, by the same mutant class as the row above — one that mints an entity from a directive's ARGUMENT — combined with the anchor/scrub mutants that make this decoy match at all (both verified to fire on the edge side). The earlier wording called it unreachable on the grounds that componentNameFromPath never reads the file; that is a fact about the SHIPPED code, not about the mutant space, and the two were conflated. Its extra value over the row above is the source of the name: a COMMENTED-OUT directive, which is the rule-pack failure shape (internal/engine/rules/graphql/frameworks/graphql_schema.yaml does exactly this for commented-out SDL). Its `kind` was SCOPE.UIComponent until the mutant was actually run: the route being fenced mints SCOPE.Component, so the row named a kind nothing in the mutant space produces and sat unfireable beside two that fired. Found by running it, not by reading it — which is the whole argument for grading a fence rather than asserting it is unreachable.

forbidden_entities.name: IPhantom
forbidden_entities.note: #6370: the interface named inside the multi-line Razor comment. Same grading status as the row above: reachable by an argument-minting mutant, and distinct from it in that this decoy is LINE-LEADING inside its comment, so on the edge side the scrub alone rejects it. Not an unreachable fence — the earlier note said it was.
